From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: PrivInfra architecture alignment — follow-up & scheduling pulse

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the discovery call this afternoon — really helpful to understand MedAsync's latency and data-isolation constraints. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get the technical deep-dive on the calendar: 

Recap (short):
- Primary goal: private hosting for PHI-adjacent inference workloads with per-tenant VPC isolation.
- Priority: predictable p99 latency under 250ms for small-batch inference and retention controls for audit requirements.
- Constraints: strict outbound egress controls, customer-managed KMS, and potential on-prem options for a subset of customers.

Proposed next step: 90-minute architecture review (VPC/on-prem orientation + ops/runbook checklist) with our infra and SE leads (we'll bring a solutions engineer + infra architect).

Availability (PST) — if any of these work for you, I’ll lock a slot:
- Mon Nov 9, 10:00–11:30 or 13:00–14:30
- Tue Nov 10, 14:00–15:30 (preferred by our SE team)
- Thu Nov 12, 09:00–10:30 or 16:00–17:30

If none of those fit, here’s a quick poll/calendly to pick a convenient window: https://calendly.com/jordan-blake/privinfra-deepdive

Attached is a draft agenda and pre-call checklist to help your team prepare. If you expect any additional internal folks (security, network), let me know so we include them.

Looking forward — I’ll follow up in 24 hours if I don’t hear back.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

- I'll loop in Rohit (rohit@medasync.io) and Elena (elena.gomez@medasync.io, security) to the architecture review.

Before the call it would be helpful to get a short list of what you typically need from us in advance (VPC/subnet ranges, existing VPN or direct connect, AWS account IDs if applicable). Do you have a short template?

We’ll put Tue Nov 10, 14:00–15:30 PST on a tentative hold for now (I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm Rohit and Elena can make it). Attaching the agenda and a short pre-call checklist — the checklist includes the exact fields we ask for (VPC ranges, account IDs, preferred key policy).

Jordan

Looping in some SE prep notes — copying the relevant bits from our runbook so Asha knows what we'll want on the call.

Ben's pre-call checklist (summary):
- Request an existing VPC diagram (latest) and any current NAT/egress hop details.
- Confirm whether KMS is customer-managed; if so, we need the key ARN and IAM role/principal we can use for encryption in transit.
- If on-prem is in scope: public IP blocks and firewall contact for scheduled test windows.
- Expected peak qps and average request size so we can size batching and cache policies for the demo.

I'll attach a short template you can drop into an email to Rohit/Elena: network-access-template.md

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
